tax.name: South Carolina state and local taxes

note_add: Registered overnight campers pay no park admission; only visitors not registered for an overnight stay pay it (adult admission is per person, $3-8 by park). Quoted nightly rates exclude taxes and a reservation fee whose amount is not published; rates vary by season and demand rather than by a flat weekend premium. Six people per site (a single larger family may be allowed). Park reservation pages allow one trailer/RV plus one tent and at most two passenger vehicles per site; whether the RV counts as one of the two is not stated. Personal golf carts are $5 a night.

sources.quote: Visitors not registered for an overnight stay are required to pay the park admission.
$8 adults; $5/SC seniors (age 65 & older);
Rates are subject to state and local taxes, and are subject to change.
The quoted rate for each night does not include taxes or the reservation fee.
No more than six persons (or one family) may occupy the same site.
Maximum of 2 passenger vehicles per site.
Personal golf cart use incurs a $5 per night charge based on the length of your stay.

unsettled.reservation_fee: Park reservation pages say the nightly rate 'does not include taxes or the reservation fee' but no page I could read states the amount (the FAQ lists only cancellation/change administrative fees of $10).
unsettled.nonresident: No general non-resident camping rate appears on the FAQ (only resident discounts, extended to out-of-state residents at six parks), but no page says outright there is none.
unsettled.extra_vehicle: Two passenger vehicles per site on park reservation pages (Santee, Croft); no extra-vehicle charge published, and it is unclear whether the RV counts as one of the two, so no field written.
unsettled.extra_person.amount: Six-person cap only; no statement that there is no per-person charge.
unsettled.tax.percent: State plus local taxes; combined rate varies by county.

summary: SC: registered campers pay no admission, rates exclude state and local taxes, 6 people per site; reservation fee exists but its amount is unpublished.

note_add: State parks are free to enter, except a per-vehicle entrance fee ($10 a day) at the Falls Lake, Jordan Lake and Kerr Lake state recreation areas on weekends and holidays in April, May and September and daily Memorial Day to Labor Day; no page says whether registered campers there pay it. The $3 service fee is charged once per reservation (in person too) and is already inside the posted campsite prices, so it is not a separate add-on. Generally six people, two tents and two vehicles per family campsite. No weekend or holiday rate.

sources.quote: All other state parks are free to enter year-round.
A parking/vehicle entrance fee is charged at Falls Lake, Jordan Lake, and Kerr Lake state recreation areas
Entrance fees are charged per vehicle on weekends and holidays in April, May, and September,
A $3 service fee is charged for all reservations, including those made in-person.
A $3 non-refundable service fee is included in prices listed, where applicable.
Generally, there is a maximum limit of six people, two tents, and two vehicles per family campsite.
Generally, there is a maximum limit of six people, two tents, and two vehicles per family campsite.

unsettled.reservation_fee: The $3 per-reservation service fee is folded into the posted per-night prices, so neither 3 (would double-count) nor 0 (a fee is charged) is right; left in prose.
unsettled.tax: The fee page never mentions tax; no source found on whether sales tax is added or included.
unsettled.nonresident: No residency-based rate on the fee page, but it does not call itself a complete schedule and no page says there is none.
unsettled.extra_vehicle.amount: Two-vehicle cap; no extra-vehicle charge published.
unsettled.extra_person.amount: Six-person cap; no statement that there is no per-person charge.

summary: NC: free entry except the three reservoir SRAs (campers' status unstated), 6 people and 2 vehicles per site; the $3 service fee is inside posted prices.

note_add: Overnight fees include parking for the vehicles the site allows: the camping unit plus two motor vehicles (so a motorhome and two cars, or a trailer, its tow vehicle and one more), with no daily parking fee; each further vehicle pays the park's daily parking fee ($5-10 by park). Six people or one immediate family per site. The $5 transaction fee is charged once per overnight rental and covers the whole stay. Virginia sales tax is added at the locality's combined rate. No weekend premium for campsites (prime-season holiday rates apply to cabins).

sources.quote: Also, a non-refundable $5 transaction fee is charged for all overnight rentals.
The fee covers the entire stay, regardless of length.
A $5 non-refundable transaction fee and applicable Virginia sales tax will be added to all fees.
Parking fees are included in all overnight fees up to the number of vehicles specified for the site rented.
Only two motor vehicles in addition to the camping unit allowed under subsection C of this section are permitted on a campsite with no additional prices.
Any additional vehicles beyond two are subject to daily parking prices
Occupancy of each campsite shall be limited to not more than six persons or one immediate family
Claytor Lake $27 $32

unsettled.extra_vehicle.amount: Extra vehicles pay the park's daily parking fee, $5-10 by park; a range, so no amount.
unsettled.extra_person.amount: Six-person cap; DCR's fee regulation (4VAC5-36) was repealed 2025-12-17, so there is no complete schedule to show there is no per-person charge.
unsettled.tax.percent: Sales tax at the local combined rate, which varies by region; DCR does not state a percent.

summary: VA: $5 per-stay transaction fee confirmed, sales tax added, campers' parking included for the camping unit plus two vehicles, 6 people max; nonresident +$5 verified for standard sites.

sources.quote: Up to six people can camp under the same authorization.

unsettled.reservation_fee: The authorization and Access Permits are bought through Go Outdoors Virginia or a license agent; no DWR page states whether a transaction or agent fee is added.
unsettled.tax: No source says whether the $10 authorization or $4 permits carry tax.
unsettled.extra_person: Each extra person 17+ costs the $4/day Access Permit, which the entrance key already holds; the authorization covers up to six (more if one household), already in prereq_pass. Writing an extra_person amount would double-count.
unsettled.extra_vehicle: 4VAC15-20-155 and the DWR camping page say nothing about extra-vehicle charges (only that camping vehicles must not fill the parking area).

summary: wma:VA: nothing new settled; the per-person charge is already the Access Permit, no source on vehicle, tax or transaction fees.

note_add: No entrance fee anywhere in the state park system. At most two motor vehicles and one camping unit per campsite (58CSR32 s2.5), so a motorhome towing a car fills the limit. The site fee covers no other fee-charged facility. The booking site adds taxes and fees to online reservations (stated for lodge rooms); the amounts for campsites are not published.

sources.quote: With no entrance fees across the West Virginia State Park system,
No more than two motor vehicles are permitted on a campsite at any time.
The campsite rental fee does not include the use of any other facilities or services for which a fee or rental is charged.
Please note that taxes and fees are charged on all on-line reservations.

unsettled.reservation_fee: The only statement ('taxes and fees are charged on all on-line reservations') is on a lodge-room deal page and gives no amount; no campsite reservation-fee figure published.
unsettled.tax: Same lodge-room page says taxes are charged online; a 2017 Watoga campground form said tax was included in the campsite fee. Conflicting and neither is a current campsite statement.
unsettled.nonresident: None on any official page, but no page says there is none (the existing note says the same).
unsettled.extra_person: 58CSR32 sets no headcount limit and publishes no per-person charge.
unsettled.extra_vehicle.amount: Two-vehicle cap; no extra-vehicle charge published.

summary: WV: no entrance fees statewide, two motor vehicles per campsite; reservation fee, tax and rates still only inside the booking engine.

note_add: Campers pay no daily entrance fee and need no day-use reservation (display the camper hang tag). The non-refundable transaction fee is $6.25 per reservation and $4.75 to change or cancel (set in 2017; DNR said in March 2026 the new booking system kept the same fee structure); Assateague was the 2017 exception at $6.25 per night. Posted base rates exclude transaction and other applicable fees. Six people per site (children count), normally two sleeping units, two vehicles if they fit on the pad; parks may differ.

sources.quote: transaction fees will be reduced to $6.25 per reservation and $4.75 per transaction
(except for Assateague State Park, which will remain $6.25 per night)
the transaction fee structure is the same as under the previous system.
Base rate does not include transaction or other applicable fees
Do I need to pay the daily entrance fee if I am camping? No, you may enjoy all of the park amenities while camping.
No, as long as they have a separate reservation for camping.
A maximum of six people at a time (children count as people).
Two vehicles are allowed to park at each site as long as they fit on the paved surface.

unsettled.tax: No DNR page mentions tax on camping.
unsettled.nonresident: Current service-charge page lists single camping amounts with no out-of-state rate; a 2020 Gambrill rate sheet showed non-residents +$1 and Elk Neck's page shows +$1 (entry 659 carries it). Not settled agency-wide.
unsettled.surcharges.weekend: Every MD state entry carries weekend +$1 from booking-site prices (2026-10-12) and the 2020 Gambrill sheet shows Fri/Sat +$1, but the current DNR service-charge page publishes no weekend rate, so no agency-wide primary statement.
unsettled.extra_vehicle.amount: Two-vehicle cap; no extra-vehicle charge published.
unsettled.extra_person.amount: Six-person cap; no statement that there is no per-person charge.

summary: MD: $6.25 per-reservation transaction fee, campers pay no entrance fee, 6 people and 2 vehicles per site.
